combo_label: At the Opticians × Volcanoes × The Canterbury Tales

entries.clue: Shut and open both eyes in an instant, wetting them as you go
Dark rock that cooled into the hexagonal columns of the Giant's Causeway
Garden of England, the county holding the city they ride towards
Geoffrey who began the work about 1387 and died in 1400 with it unfinished
Little clamshell you snap your pair into, then leave in the car
Clouding of the eye's own lens, cleared by a surgeon in a short operation
Herald's sleeveless overcoat, and the name of the inn where they set out
Great church of a bishop; the one at their journey's end held the martyr's bones
Sleeping for now though not dead, of a bulb in winter or a quiet mountain
Rounded cap over St Paul's, or a swelling bulge of stiff cooling rock
London's underground railway, or the hollow passage a molten stream leaves behind
Cloistered brother here more fond of hunting and greyhounds than of his Rule
Casual British shortening for the pair you push back up your nose
